title: 云原生控制面与 Agentic AI：从缓存、弹性到推理效率
english: Recent updates highlight two connected operational priorities: predictable cloud-native control planes and efficient AI workflows. The Kubernetes Blog explains how controller-runtime Cache works and why a clearer internal model helps Go controller authors avoid production surprises as load grows. A CNCF post describes how health checks can wake scale-to-zero services, and presents ProbeResponse as an approach to keep services idle while satisfying load balancers and uptime monitors. OpenAI reports that retaining reasoning and enabling compaction improved GPT-5.6 results and efficiency on ARC-AGI-3. Its other updates emphasize efficiency across inference and agentic workflows, as well as AI coding agents for scientific computing.
chinese: 本组信息的共同主题是：系统效率不仅取决于业务逻辑，也取决于运行时机制。对 Kubernetes 运维开发而言，controller-runtime 的缓存行为会影响控制器与 API Server 的交互方式；负载增长时，理解其内部模型有助于避免生产环境中的意外。对于 scale-to-zero 服务，健康检查可能反向触发实例唤醒，因此需要同时满足流量入口、监控与空闲弹性的约束。AI 侧则强调保留推理、压缩以及面向 agentic workflow 的推理效率；科学计算场景中，AI 编码 Agent 正被用于软件现代化与研究协作。
why_it_matters: 这直接关联云原生平台工程与 AIOps：一方面，需要以缓存、探针和弹性策略降低控制面及闲置服务的资源成本；另一方面，Agent Infra 需要把模型推理效率、上下文管理和工作流设计作为可观测、可优化的运行要素。对资深运维开发者而言，Kubernetes 控制器机制、scale-to-zero 行为和 AI Agent 工作负载治理正在形成交叉能力栈。
interview_expression: I focus on the runtime behavior behind cloud-native abstractions, especially cache consistency, probe side effects, and control-plane load. For AI agents, I would treat inference efficiency and workflow observability as operational concerns, not only model concerns.

vocabulary.meaning: 协调器；Kubernetes 控制器中负责将实际状态收敛到期望状态的逻辑。
vocabulary.example: The reconciler updates resources until the observed state matches the desired state.

vocabulary.meaning: 缩容至零；在无请求或空闲时将服务实例数降为零的弹性模式。
vocabulary.example: A scale-to-zero service should remain idle until real traffic arrives.

vocabulary.meaning: 压缩；此处指通过压缩处理提高推理或工作流效率。
vocabulary.example: Compaction can improve efficiency in an agentic workflow.

sources.title: How the controller-runtime Cache Actually Works, and Why Your Controller Does Not Crash the API Server
sources.summary:
Kubernetes has long been the default platform for distributed workloads, and writing your own controller for it is now a matter of a few hours. The common path — Golang, using kubebuilder on top of controller-runtime — gives you a project scaffold, types, and a reconciler. For typical scenarios that is more than enough. But as soon as load grows or the controller starts behaving in ways you did not expect, a whole class of edge cases shows up. Most of them trace back to the same root cause: a fuzzy mental model of how controller-runtime works inside. If you write Kubernetes controllers in Go, this article should help you build a coherent picture and avoid expensive surprises in production.

This article walks through the internals of controller-runtime and, along the way, shows which architectural decisions are baked into Kuber
